subject_name: Aircraft Wiring Practices (Electrical wiring and Interface system)
topic: Main rotor movements, symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook's joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle
syllabus_extract: Main rotor movements, symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook’s joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle concepts.
specific_objectives: 12.1.5.1 Trainee will be able to understand Main rotor movements, symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook’s joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle concepts.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of rotor dynamics diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What are the primary movements of a main rotor?
Define symmetry of lift in rotor systems.
List the factors causing flapping and dragging.

development.content:
Main rotor movements overview
Symmetry of lift feathering
Flapping and dragging dynamics
Hook's joint effect analysis
Flapping to equality principle

Phase lag concept explanation
Advance angle mechanics
Rotor system equilibrium
Lift distribution analysis
Dynamic stability factors

Integration of rotor movements
Application of phase lag theory
Summary of flapping dynamics
Review of hook's joint effect
Final concept reinforcement

summary_questions: Explain the relationship between phase lag and advance angle.
Describe how flapping contributes to rotor symmetry.
Identify the role of the hook's joint in rotor dynamics.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how rotor movements affect hovering and forward flight, linking concepts to LP 06 syllabus.

pft_rows.syllabus: Hovering and forward flight, take off and climb to free air hover, vertical decent ground effect ground cushion re circulation effects.
